newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's Bankside to demerge members' agency.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's Bankside to demerge members' agency.

text.p: Lloyd's of London underwriting operation Bankside will have to demerge its members' agency business before it is acquired by LIMIT, according to insurance industry sources.

LIMIT (London Insurance Market Investment Trust) wants to buy Bankside as part of an expansion that also includes the takeover of the Janson Green managing agency. It is already the biggest corporate investor in the Lloyd's insurance market.

LIMIT does not want the members' agency -- which is responsible for recruiting the Names that traditionally fund the insurance market -- because it is not central to the business of underwriting insurance.
Industry sources said the demerger is likely to be decided by shareholders at an extraordinary meeting next month.
There are about 130 shareholders in Bankside, which manages eight syndicates with a total capacity of 403 million stg.
The biggest are directors and employees of the unquoted company.

Other underwriting agents in Lloyd's have already separated themselves from members' agencies as the insurance market consolidates and moves towards closer alignment between the underwriting agents and corporate capital.
There are about thirty members' agencies and rationalisation is expected to reduce this number to between ten and twenty.

In July, four members' agencies -- R F Kershaw, Castle, Marlborough, and Holman Macleod -- joined forces to create a single group handling nearly 500 million stg in capacity this year on behalf of 870 Names. Capacity is the amount of business the market can underwrite measured in terms of premium income.
LIMIT earlier on Thursday declared its 18.6 million stg takeover of Janson Green unconditional.
It intends eventually to float both managing agencies on the London stock market. LIMIT backs 610 million stg in capacity.
